ruling.recommended_action: Refund $6.68 to the rider as a Ryde voucher (unexempted detour 4.74 km × $1.4098/km meter units) and note the driver's RD-1 route-duty breach; no account flag required.
ruling.reasoning:
Safety screen: chat #1/#2 are a route arrangement, the driver's statement and the complaint contain no threat, abuse, harassment or dangerous-driving allegation → safety_concern none.

Service type: RydeTAXI (metered), so detour distance feeds the fare (RD-2 meter branch, policy §0).

Segments: one off-route segment, 08:42–08:54, 7.24 km where the optimal route covers 2.50 km, +4.74 km, up to 1568 m off the optimal route [F3]. The rider did consent before the segment began — 08:40 "可以，走 Balestier Road 吧" [F9] precedes the 08:42 segment start, and the driver's written statement [F11] is a claim only (G11), so my finding rests on the chat alone.

RD-5 scope reading: the consent is a named-road consent to Balestier Road. Nothing in the record ties the driven segment to Balestier Road — no roadside stop, no location message, no road-name fact — so under RD-5 + G13 the segment's coverage is undetermined rather than exempt. It is also not placed elsewhere, so "named_road_elsewhere" does not apply. Per G13, an undetermined finding that changes the amount goes to a human.

Amount the undefined segment would carry (RD-2): 4.74 km × this trip's per-km rate. F4 gives the trip's own rate as $1.4098/km → 4.74 × 1.4098 = $6.6825 → $6.68. I refund that meter-difference because the driver cannot show the consent he relies on (Ryde places the burden of "mutual agreement" on the driver, A7); the rest of the excess distance in F4 (5.12 km total) is not refunded. Waiting fee $0.11 [F5] is a meter-derived amount and is not refunded (RD-3(c)). No traffic incident on the optimal route [F15], and the speed band 2 on Central Expressway [F12] is only corroborative and cannot exempt a segment on its own (RD-4(b), G3); in any event no record ties the driven segment to the CTE being avoided. No ERP/toll discrepancy (FARE-2 not triggered; no tolls fact).

Flag: driver profile shows 0 disputes upheld in 90 d [F18], so RD-6 is not met; no flag_account. Rider profile [F17] does not decide anything.

Evidence status: sufficient for the elements I applied (timestamps present [F10], GPS coverage and fare breakdown present), but because the RD-5 tie is undetermined under G13 and the undetermined finding changes the amount, the case should be routed to a human reviewer before the voucher executes. Ruling issued as refund_partial with the escalation note.
ruling.escalation_reason: G13 undetermined segment affecting the amount — refund computed at $6.68 and referred for human confirmation of the RD-5 consent scope.

segment_findings.reason: Rider consented before the segment began (08:40 message vs 08:42 segment start), but the consent names only Balestier Road and no record (stop, location message, road-name fact) ties the driven 08:42–08:54 segment to Balestier Road; per RD-5 + G13 coverage is undetermined, not exempt. Nothing places the segment elsewhere, so the driver-errand/elsewhere reading also fails on this record.

rejected_claims.reason: Driver's post-trip statement of verbal agreement is a claim, not consent; consent must be the rider's own message before the detour (RD-5, G11). It adds nothing beyond the chat.
Speed band 2 on Central Expressway is corroborative only and cannot by itself exempt a segment (RD-4(b), G3), and no record ties the driven segment to the CTE avoidance.
Rider profile facts do not decide the case (profile facts never decide alone).
Driver profile shows 0 upheld disputes in 90 d, so the RD-6 repeated-violation flag condition is not met.

ruling.evidence_gap: No record tying the driven off-route segment to the consented Balestier Road (no roadside stop, no location/road-name fact): per G13 the segment's coverage is undetermined and, as it changes the refund amount, the case should be confirmed by a human reviewer.
